where: A homestead in the City of Austin and Austin ISD.
input_label: Appraised value of your home (from the appraisal district)
split_note: Each unit’s rate is split into its maintenance-and-operations (M&O) part and its interest-and-sinking (I&S) part — the I&S part pays debt.
rollback_note: Texas’s version of the “no-raise” rate is the no-new-revenue rate: the rate that would bring each taxing unit the same tax as last year from the same properties. Texas law makes each unit publish it; going above the higher voter-approval rate generally needs an election.
hearing: Texas taxing units adopt rates each August and September after public hearings; school districts and colleges set their own.
limits: Homestead exemptions shown are the general ones; over-65, disabled and veteran exemptions and school tax ceilings aren’t modeled.
Homes inside a municipal utility district or emergency services district pay more; this example has neither.
